issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to aggregate animals using a List implemented with an ArrayList and to provide a getter/setter for that List, but the solution implements the animals collection as a Queue backed by a LinkedList (Queue<Animal> animals). This is a structural type mismatch: the field and its getter/setter types differ from the specified List/ArrayList design. Students following the instructions to use List/ArrayList will see a different design in the reference solution and may be confused or fail tests that expect the List type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm implementation match the specification: declare the animals attribute as a List<Animal>, initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor, and provide getter/setter with the List<Animal> type. Update the solution repository accordingly (replace Queue/LinkedList usage with List/ArrayList) so template, problem statement, and solution are consistent.

issues.description: The template's private singFarmSongVerse method currently has its Animal parameter commented out (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), whereas the UML/problem specification and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse to accept an Animal parameter. This mismatch between the template signature and the intended design can confuse students about the required method signature and parameter usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment and include the Animal parameter in the template method signature so it matches the UML and solution: private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Ensure the template body uses the passed-in animal to print verse details. This aligns the template with the problem specification and the solution.

issues.description: The Problem Statement and UML specify that Farm should maintain its animals as a List<Animal> and explicitly instruct using an ArrayList initialized in the no-arg constructor. The Solution implementation, however, defines the same conceptual attribute as a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList (private Queue<Animal> animals), which diverges from the expected type and concrete collection class. The Template file also contains a TODO for implementing Farm but does not provide an animals attribute. This inconsistent typing of the same conceptual entity ('the collection of animals in the farm') across artifacts can confuse students mapping the UML/requirements to the code (e.g., List vs Queue, ArrayList vs LinkedList) and may cause misunderstandings about which collection type and APIs they should use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Farm implementation with the problem statement and UML: declare the field as List<Animal> animals (not Queue) and initialize it as new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor. Update getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if Queue semantics are intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify Queue and LinkedList consistently.
